source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the normal serum creatinine range?
questions.rationale: Normal creatinine is 0.6–1.2 mg/dL; BUN is 7–18 mg/dL.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Serum Tests (PDF p. 74)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which preparation is ordered before a KUB x-ray?
questions.rationale: A laxative in the evening and an enema in the morning may be ordered; little or no pain is expected.
questions.quote: Bowel preparation (laxative in the evening and enema in the morning as ordered)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In what position is cystoscopy done?
questions.rationale: Cystoscopy is performed in the lithotomy position after voiding.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: After cystoscopy, which finding is expected?
questions.rationale: Blood-tinged urine, dysuria, and frequency are expected early; fever, chills, or persistent pain are reported.
questions.quote: Urine may be blood-tinged for the first and second voiding after the procedure

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which comfort measure helps after cystoscopy?
questions.rationale: Warm sitz baths relieve discomfort; fluids are increased.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: After ERCP, when may the client eat?
questions.rationale: No food or drink until the gag reflex returns, then light meals for 12–24 hours.
questions.quote: Do not allow the patient to eat or drink until the gag reflex returns

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which ERCP aftereffect should be reported immediately?
questions.rationale: Severe pain, fever, difficulty breathing, or blood expectoration are reported; sore throat and belching are expected.
questions.quote: Emphasize that any severe pain, fever, difficulty breathing, or expectoration of blood must be report

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which hemoglobin value is normal for an adult female?
questions.rationale: Normal Hgb: female 12–16 g/dL; male 13–18 g/dL.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the normal adult WBC count?

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which factor can alter bone marrow biopsy results?
questions.rationale: Recent transfusions, iron therapy, or cytotoxic agents may alter results; it is contraindicated with bleeding disorders.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bone Marrow Biopsy (PDF p. 77)
questions.quote: Recent blood transfusions, iron therapy, or administration of cytotoxic agents may alter test results

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which client is at risk with retrograde ureteropyelography?
questions.rationale: Contraindications include dye allergy, dehydration, renal failure, and multiple myeloma (reduced kidney function).
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Retrograde Ureteropyelography (PDF p. 75)
questions.quote: Multiple myeloma who may experience decreased kidney function
